A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GraphGPT based on Eulerian graph serialization and generative pre-training. All 25 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, tables, figures, and mathematical content supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GraphGPT benchmark results, component ablations, and training curves in Sections 3.2–3.5 and Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark, transfer-learning, structural-generalization, and ablation results in Tables 1–7, with additional experimental material in the appendices.

M1.justification: v1 uses a transformer decoder with next-token prediction. v2 adds an encoder using bidirectional attention and scheduled masked-token prediction, including simultaneous masking of every occurrence of a node. It also introduces cyclic node re-indexing, short/long attribute formats, and simultaneous prediction of multiple tokens per sequence position. These substantially extend the procedure beyond the GET renaming.

E1.justification: The four principal v1 datasets are retained. v2 adds Triangles counting with larger-graph tests, ogbl-citation2 link prediction, and ogbn-arxiv classification, plus Reddit-threads, internal real-world graphs, and random graphs for pre-training. The ogbl-ddi experiment reported qualitatively in v1 Appendix E.4 is absent from v2.

E2.justification: Comparator sets change substantially on retained datasets. PCQM4Mv2 gains GPS-Deep, GPS++ and GPTrans-L while losing Transformer-M and Uni-Mol+. Molpcba gains Graphormer-L, EGT-Larger, GRPE-Large and GPTrans-L. On ogbl-ppa, Node2Vec replaces DeepWalk, and MPLP and RefinedGAE are added. Og bn-proteins comparisons add GAT, AGDN and numerous graph transformers while removing UniMP, RevGNN-wide and GIPA.

E3.justification: v2 changes model configurations, sampling settings, batch sizes and learning-rate schedules. Its ogbl-ppa and ogbn-proteins pre-training budgets are 20 billion tokens, versus 25.6–50 billion and 51.2 billion respectively in v1. The main molpcba evaluation now transfers PCQM4Mv2-pretrained models. New protocols include Triangles training/validation and small/large test splits, and ogbl-citation2 negative-tail sampling and training on sampled edge subsets.

E4.justification: v2 adds structural-transfer and graph-size generalization analyses on Triangles, comparisons of pre-training corpus types and mixtures, and NTP/SMTP comparisons with unpretrained encoder and decoder controls. Figure 4 additionally compares citation-network sampling configurations. The node re-indexing ablation in v1 Table 6 is removed. The node-identity ablation remains in Table 7 with the same values, although its learning-curve analyses are removed.

E5.justification: v1 Section 3.4 explicitly calculates ogbn-proteins means and variances from three consecutive validation-selected epochs. v2 omits this explanation while continuing to report ± values. This changes statistical-method disclosure; it does not establish that run counts or the underlying estimator changed. No new seed information or formal significance testing is documented.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports PCQM4Mv2 test MAE of 0.0804, previously unavailable, and ogbl-citation2 MRR of 93.05%. The headline ogbl-ppa result changes from 67.15±1.36 for v1's large model to 76.55±0.67 for v2's XXL model under different model and training conditions. Molecular-transfer, Triangles and arxiv results are added, and protein result series are revised. Several earlier NTP and node-identity results remain, while the negative ogbl-ddi finding disappears.

T1.justification: v2 adds the cyclic-index definition i' = (i+r) mod N and sequence-length relations for the short, long and prolonged representations in Section 2.2.1 and Figure 1. The existing Chinese Postman/Eulerian argument for reversible serialization up to isomorphism is retained. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from an NTP-trained decoder to a GET framework supporting both decoder and encoder pre-training. The abstract and introduction raise the demonstrated scaling claim from 400 million-plus to approximately two billion parameters. The conclusion also elevates structural and molecular transferability from v1's proposed possibilities to claimed empirical capabilities.

C2.justification: v2 interprets new experiments as evidence of cross-dataset structural transfer and within-domain molecular transfer, which v1 Appendix G largely proposed as future possibilities. It adds explanations involving real-world graph patterns, pre-training diversity, parameter allocation and possible saturation of 2D molecular information. The ogbl-ddi-based caution about small dense graphs is removed, and the dataset-size limitation is reframed around ogbn-arxiv.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the shared training recipe with extensive dataset/model-specific configuration Tables 11–15, documenting optimizer settings, dropout, schedules, precision, layer scaling and EMA. Hardware changes from V100-32G to A800-80G, and compute estimates are revised. It newly states that 86% of PCQM4Mv2 validation data is added to training after tuning. Both versions promise future code/checkpoint release, but v2 removes v1's repository address; the new internal corpus lacks access instructions.

R1.justification: v2 broadens its methodological positioning to masked generative learning through MaskGIT and multi-token prediction through Gloeckle et al. It substantially expands references and comparisons to graph transformers and link-prediction research, including GPTrans, GPS++, Polynormer and RefinedGAE. It also removes v1's assertion that using transformer encoders prevents self-supervised pre-training.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and approach are extensively rewritten into labeled explanations and procedural lists. The title and author list change. Limitations move from Appendix G into main Section 4, and tokenization examples formerly distributed across task appendices are consolidated into Appendix D, followed by reorganized task-specific experimental appendices.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout for the main text and references. Figure 1 is redrawn from a full training workflow into a serialization and attribute-format diagram. Benchmark tables are reordered and restructured, including paired-dataset columns for edge and node tasks. A Triangles table and detailed configuration tables are added, while several earlier ablation and training curves are removed or replaced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for transferable graph pre-training: structural and molecular transfer proposed in v1 Appendix G become reported experiments in Tables 2–3, and Table 6 adds encoder/decoder and pre-training comparisons. The previously missing PCQM4Mv2 test result and detailed training configurations also improve assessability. Removing the re-indexing ablation, negative ogbl-ddi finding and epoch-aggregation explanation reduces transparency, and the internal corpus remains poorly specified. Nevertheless, the direct validation of central transfer claims and fuller experimental documentation provide a substantial net improvement.
